speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Health whether the Ministry can allow any patient regardless of prognosis to participate in the pilot for Pre-implantation Genetic Screening (PGS) so as to increase the number of patients enrolled under the pilot study.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the average cost for participating in the pilot for Pre-implantation Genetic Screening (PGS); and (b) whether the Ministry can consider completely subsidising these costs so as to increase the number of patients enrolled under the pilot study.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These eligibility criteria are not set arbitrarily but developed with reference to available international evidence and aligned with clinical practices in overseas assisted reproduction centres.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: PGS is a technically complex procedure which carries potential risks, including damage to the embryos during the biopsy, with impact on their subsequent development, and should be reserved for women who fulfil the eligibility criteria to undergo the procedure.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: PGS is performed together with in vitro fertilisation (IVF).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For IVF, patients can receive Government support through the Assisted Reproduction Technology co-funding scheme as well as tap on their MediSave.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: MOH will continue to assess the clinical effectiveness of PGS, including looking at overseas data and collecting more data from cases here in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: MOH will also explore options for co-sharing of costs of PGS for patients who are keen to be part of the study, but have affordability concerns.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: If PGS is included as a mainstream healthcare service, it will then be assessed for means-tested subsidies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand, as the Parliamentary Secretary mentioned, over 300 people enrolled for PGS but only about a hundred actually did PGS.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, could I ask MOH what are the main reasons why people did not proceed with PGS.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And, two, what steps MOH is taking to increase the enrolment of PGS and decrease the the drop-out rate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And third, the feedback on the ground is that there is a cost issue.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I hope MOH can look into this and fully subsidise this so that more people can participate in this trial and, hopefully, we can then nationalise it to benefit more people.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Prior to the start of the pilot, the evaluation team had determined that the target of 300 patients with PGS testing would be needed to achieve statistical significance.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Almost half of the patients changed their minds after the ovarian stimulation and fertilisation stage, and proceeded with embryo transfer directly without performing PGS or decided to freeze their embryos instead.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Other patients did not proceed with a biopsy due to medical reasons, such as poor quality of the blastocyst or embryo arrest.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As the Member rightly pointed out, we do need a bit more data to fully study this to understand its clinical effectiveness.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: MOH is doing its best to try and assist and support as many patients as possible to go through this process and this remains something that we will continue to review.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And as far as the cost is concerned, this is something that we understand is a challenge.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For the patients who really need support for this, we will look into this matter.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But as it is at the moment, there is limited and inconclusive evidence on the clinical effectiveness.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We do need to proceed carefully with this process because there is also an impact on the embryo.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There is a low risk, but there is still risk to the embryo and we do need to make sure that the right people proceed for this procedure.
